retrieval of emotionally relevant information is associated with bidirectional interactions between amygdala and hippocampus, which are modulated by the orbitofrontal cortices.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the integration of mnemonic information with emotional content during retrieval involves bidirectional interactions between the amygdala and the hippocampus, under modulatory influence from the orbitofrontal and medial prefrontal cortex.
the integration of memory and emotion is not a simple function of the amygdala, but a complex interaction between the amygdala and the hippocampus.
the brain regions that are involved in memory retrieval are also involved in the integration of memory and emotion, and that the nature of the integration depends on the task demands.
